assertions.text: The response identifies at least one sentence in the plan's self-description ('Who I am') as generic enough to be true of almost anyone, rather than specific to Marcus.
The response points out that the plan's claim that Marcus finishes what he starts is contradicted by the abandoned novel attempts in his own background notes.
The response states that all three options rest on the same underlying bet — fiction income arriving within a few years — rather than being genuinely different alternatives.
The response disputes the plan's assumed £40k advance or year-three writing income as unsupported by typical debut outcomes or by Marcus's publication record.
The response states, with arithmetic from the budget figures, that the household runway is materially shorter than the 18 months the plan claims.
The response identifies that option C's relocation for the 2027-28 academic year conflicts with the written agreement not to move house before Maya finishes her GCSEs.
The response points out that the plan names no observable sign by which Marcus would conclude the path is failing, treating 'no wobbles, no exit ramps' as a defect rather than a strength.
The response commits to a specific recommendation for what Marcus should do next, rather than presenting options neutrally.
The response proposes at least one concrete action Marcus can start within a month that tests the writing path without resigning.
The response cites at least one specific project or review detail from Marcus's background notes when assessing what he demonstrably finishes.
The response stops short of telling Marcus to give up on writing altogether.
